title: Curriculum design templates for Mac: how to speed up your course development
metaTitle: Curriculum Design Templates for Mac: Speed Up Course Development
description: Learn how to use curriculum design templates on your Mac to manage course development, research, and administrative tasks more efficiently.
intro: Curriculum design templates help you organize complex learning objectives and content structures on your Mac. You can use these templates to maintain consistency across multiple course projects while reducing the time spent on repetitive formatting tasks.
tldr: Use structured curriculum design templates to standardize your course development process.

blocks.text: Why curriculum design templates matter for your workflow

Curriculum design templates are more than just pretty documents. They act as a blueprint for your learning architecture. When you build a template in Google Docs or Microsoft Word, you define the structure for every lesson, module, and assessment. This ensures that every project starts from a solid foundation. On a Mac, you can keep these templates in a dedicated folder. Use Finder to tag them as templates so you can find them quickly with ⌘ Space.

Many designers struggle with the administrative weight of their role. You might spend hours formatting documents or checking alignment. By using a consistent template, you remove the guesswork from your daily routine. You can also create templates for your project management trackers. If you use a spreadsheet, set up your columns for milestones, SME feedback, and deadlines once. Then duplicate that file for each new project.
Managing your time as a curriculum designer

You likely manage three projects at once. This requires you to shift your focus often. When you are in the middle of writing content, an email about a project update can break your concentration. Instead of stopping your work to reply, keep a list of tasks. Use Apple Reminders on your Mac to track these items. You can ask Lazur to add a reminder while you keep working on your course content.

Collaboration with subject matter experts takes up a large portion of your week. You need to review their inputs and translate them into learning materials. Keep a log of these interactions. If you use a shared document, ensure you track changes clearly. This prevents confusion later in the development cycle. Always follow your employer rules regarding the handling of sensitive client or student data.

blocks.text: How to use your Mac to speed up development

Your Mac has built-in tools that help you work faster. Learn the keyboard shortcuts for your preferred apps. In Google Docs, use ⌘ ⌥ C to copy formatting and ⌘ ⌥ V to paste it. This is a small change but it saves minutes every hour. When you are stuck on a technical step, ask Lazur to point at the menu item you need. This keeps your hands on the keyboard and your eyes on the content.

If you use virtualization software like Parallels to run Windows apps, keep your Mac shortcuts in mind. You can map common functions to your Mac keyboard. This makes the transition between macOS and your Windows authoring tools feel more natural. Remember to keep your software updated to the latest version to ensure compatibility. Check the documentation for your specific authoring tool for the most efficient workflow tips.
Refining your research and drafting process

Research is a core part of your day. You need to synthesize information from many sources. Use your browser to open multiple tabs for your research. If you are using the Lazur Chrome extension, you can ask for a summary of a complex topic. This helps you grasp the main points without reading every page in detail. Use this information to draft your course content directly in your document.

When drafting, use dictation to get your ideas down quickly. Hold the fn key and speak your thoughts. This is useful for outlining modules or writing draft copy for your slides. You can then polish the text once it is on the page. This approach helps you overcome writer block and keeps your momentum going throughout the day. Always review the output to ensure it meets your quality standards.

SMEs provide the content, but you provide the structure. This dynamic requires clear communication. Set expectations early about how you will receive feedback. Ask them to provide comments in your documents rather than sending long emails. This keeps the conversation tied to specific parts of the curriculum. Use the comment feature in Google Docs to keep track of these discussions.

If an SME is unclear, ask them to explain the concept in a meeting. Take notes during the call. You can use Lazur to dictate these notes in real time. This ensures you capture their expertise without missing important details. Once the meeting ends, organize your notes into your design template. This keeps your project moving forward without delay.

faq.question: What is the best way to start a new curriculum project?
faq.answer: Start by opening a verified curriculum design template. This ensures your project follows your established standards from the first minute. Then, outline your learning objectives and set up your project tracker.

faq.question: How can I manage multiple projects on my Mac?
faq.answer: Use separate spaces for each project. You can switch between them with ⌃ ➡️ or ⌃ ⬅️. Use Apple Reminders to keep track of deadlines for each project.

faq.question: Can I use voice commands to help with instructional design?
faq.answer: Yes. You can use voice commands to manage your calendar, set reminders, or search for information. You can also use dictation to draft content quickly.
